item.title: Saudi Arabia accuses Houthis of targeting Mecca, calls it a 'red line'
item.description:
Muslim pilgrims completing Hajj rituals at Islam's holiest site in Mecca, Saudi Arabia, on May 30, 2026. —Ali Atmaca—Anadolu via Getty Images Saudi Arabia on Wednesday accused the Iran-backed Houthis of an attempted attack on Mecca, the holiest city in Islam and a site of pilgrimage for Muslims worldwide. Colonel Turki Al-Malki, spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition forces in Yemen, said that the Houthis launched a drone toward Mecca on Tuesday evening, but it was shot down by the Saudi Air Defense Forces before entering the city’s restricted airspace. “The security of the Two Holy Mosques and the pilgrims is a red line,” said Al-Malki, who warned that the Saudi-led coalition “will not hesitate to take the necessary and deterrent measures” against the Houthis. Riyadh referenced a previous similar incident from July 2017, in which it accused the Houthis of targeting Mecca. The Houthis…

item.title: 'We Are Not Into Bestiality,' FBI Director Kash Patel Tells Members of Congress
item.description:
"We are not into bestiality," FBI Director Kash Patel told members of Congress yesterday, moments after assuring them that they were "not going to disqualify" any of the agency's "great canines" for engaging in sexual activity with FBI agents. I'm sorry— what? After watching this exchange from the hearing , I wondered for a moment if journalist Aaron Ruper, who had shared the clip, hadn't been taken in somehow by a deepfake. But no, it's real. And as far as I can tell, it's not actually a defense of human-to-canine coupling, thank goodness. It's just Patel handling questions about recent FBI policy changes in pretty much the worst way possible. Let's back up a moment. In August, the Associated Press reported that the FBI would no longer bar the hiring of agents who had paid for sex—with a human, I guess I should clarify—in the past.
